cases.question: Profile only the decode workers of my DGD vllm-disagg in namespace perf-test for 60 seconds while my benchmark runs. Nsight Operator is already installed.
cases.ground_truth: Check the real pod labels first. Write a per-test profile config with only a decode rule that selects the DGD name label plus the decode label the pods carry: nvidia.com/dynamo-component-type decode, or nvidia.com/dynamo-sub-component-type decode for workers that kept type worker across an operator upgrade. Use one literal tag, apply it before the pods are created, confirm one collection agent per decode pod, open one window with profiler-start --delay and --duration 60, and poll ls until every decode pod has a report with kernel rows.
expected_behavior: Check which profile-config fields the API server accepts and server-dry-run the config

Inspect the real pod labels, then select on nvidia.com/dynamo-graph-deployment-name plus the decode label they carry: the lowercase decode type, or the decode sub-component type on workers that kept type worker
Ask before restarting running pods, because only pods created after the config are profiled
Derive expected pods from the DGD, not from registered agents
Use profiler-start with a warm-up delay and a duration of 300 seconds or less
Poll ls until every decode pod has a report and check GPU reports for kernel rows

cases.question: Nsight Operator with auto-provisioning is already running on our cluster. I just want a quick nsys look at the frontend and aggregated workers of my DGD qwen-agg in namespace demo, using Nsight's Dynamo helper.
cases.ground_truth: Run nsight_operator_dynamo.py -n demo configure with --deployment-name qwen-agg, --components frontend worker in lowercase, and --nsys-profile-args without --pytorch=autograd-nvtx; do not pass --gpu-metrics or run install. Recreate the pods after asking, confirm one agent per pod on the default tag, capture with nsight_operator.py --tag default, and run unconfigure when done.
expected_behavior: Use the helper's configure subcommand with -n before the subcommand
Pass --deployment-name and lowercase component types
Override --nsys-profile-args to leave out --pytorch=autograd-nvtx
Do not pass --gpu-metrics and do not run the helper's install or uninstall
Use the default tag with nsight_operator.py and verify every expected pod has a report
Remove the helper's config with unconfigure after the reports are verified

cases.question: I ran Nsight's Dynamo helper with --components Frontend Backend and none of my Dynamo pods got injected. Why?
cases.ground_truth: The helper compares the values with the lowercase nvidia.com/dynamo-component-type label; Frontend is a component name and Dynamo has no backend type. Use lowercase types such as frontend, worker, prefill, or decode, then recreate the pods.
expected_behavior: Explain that component types are lowercase and Frontend is a component name
Check the real pod labels with kubectl get pods --show-labels
Recommend lowercase types and recreating the pods after the config is applied

cases.question: Profile the CPU side of the frontend and its KV router, with Dynamo's own NVTX ranges.
cases.ground_truth: Select the frontend type label only (the KV router runs inside the frontend by default), use the CPU tool config without CUDA tracing, and set DYN_ENABLE_RUST_NVTX=1 on Dynamo 1.6.0 or newer images before the pods start.
expected_behavior: Select the frontend with the frontend type label
Use OS runtime, NVTX, and Python sampling without CUDA tracing
Set DYN_ENABLE_RUST_NVTX=1 before the pods start and note it needs Dynamo 1.6.0 or newer
Select a standalone router by its component name only if the user runs one

cases.question: The window ended two minutes ago but ls shows reports for only two of my three workers. Can I delete the DGD now?
cases.ground_truth: Do not delete the DGD yet. Keep polling ls within a bounded wait, check status for the missing pod's collection agent, and if it never reports, mark the capture incomplete and check injection for that pod.
expected_behavior: Keep the DGD until every expected pod has a report; if the bounded wait ends first, check status and injection, mark the capture incomplete, and only then allow cleanup
Check status and injection for the missing pod
Report the capture as incomplete rather than presenting partial results
